ce_bugs.text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — Concurrent or replayed credential webhooks can both miss findFirst and create duplicate credentials, after which later updates select an arbitrary copy.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15 — Credential-sync responses are returned as raw Fetch Responses even though Google and HubSpot callers consume provider token objects, so enabling the endpoint breaks their refresh contract.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — The purported generic token schema uses Zod objects as property names and therefore strips ordinary expiry fields, so consumers cannot receive the documented access-token-and-expiry response contract.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — The computed Zod key becomes a literal key, so credential sync strips expiry and provider fields before the refreshed credential is saved.
packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — Credential-sync calls return a Fetch Response rather than a HubSpot token body, leaving `expiresIn` and `accessToken` undefined during refresh.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — This untyped helper returns incompatible Fetch and provider SDK response shapes, so consumers such as HubSpot treat a Response as a token object when credential sync is enabled.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — Credential-sync refreshes return a Fetch Response without `.data`, so expired Google credentials are silently reused after the resulting TypeError.

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — Credential-sync refreshes return a Fetch Response rather than a HubSpot token payload, so the refresh stores unusable token fields and cannot authenticate subsequent calls.

packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:84 — The sync endpoint's documented flat token response cannot satisfy Lark's provider-specific `data.*` refresh envelope, so every synced Lark refresh fails.

packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:84 — A synced response with an expiry date but no `expires_in` is persisted without the existing refresh token and is immediately treated as expired, breaking future Teams refreshes.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:101 — The new refresh result is saved but the jsforce connection is still constructed with the pre-refresh access token, so requests continue using an expired credential.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The new credential-sync fetch has no cancellation or timeout, allowing an unresponsive sync service to indefinitely block token refreshes and dependent calendar operations.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The credential-sync request sends no authentication, so the configured peer cannot distinguish Cal.com from an unauthenticated caller requesting a user's token.
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — An unset webhook secret makes an absent request header compare equal and bypasses the webhook's intended secret check.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:100 — [100/P1] `data: { key },` — `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns Zod’s `{ success, data }` wrapper, so this persists the wrapper rather than credential keys and breaks subsequent credential reads.

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — [100/P1] `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(` — enabled sync supplies a Fetch Response where following code requires HubSpot token fields, preventing refresh.

docs/tasks/task-001.md:2 — [100/P1] `Review the change.` — the task supplies no requirements, acceptance criteria, or verification expectations, so the OAuth credential-sync implementation cannot be shown to cover intended integrations or success/failure behavior.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17 — [100/P1] `export default async function handler(req: NextApiRequest, res: NextApiResponse) {` — the new credential-sync webhook’s create/update/error behavior has no corresponding test or validation change, leaving the central sync contract unverified.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — [100/P1] `[z.string().toString()]: z.number(),` — this creates a required literal `"[object Object]"` field instead of accepting any numeric expiry, so every normal credential-sync response is rejected.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:100 — [100/P1] `data: { key },` — persisting the Zod `{ success, data }` wrapper rather than the credential payload corrupts Google credentials after their first refresh.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — [100/P1] `const token = res?.data;` — the sync branch returns a Fetch Response with no `.data`, so Google refresh dereferences undefined and falls back to an expired client.

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — [100/P1] `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(` — the sync branch supplies a Fetch Response rather than HubSpot token fields, causing invalid expiry/access-token persistence and failed authorization.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:105 — [100/P1] `instanceUrl: credentialKey.instance_url,` — after persisting refreshed tokens, the connection still uses stale credential values, so expired Salesforce calls still fail.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — [75/P2] `const response = await fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, {` — refresh across enabled integrations now depends on one unbounded shared request with no timeout or fallback, so a hung sync endpoint can stall calendar/video operations system-wide.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — [100/P1] `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` — when credential sharing is enabled but the secret is unset, an omitted header compares undefined to undefined and permits arbitrary credential create/overwrite by supplied user ID.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — [75/P1] `const response = await fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId: userId.toString(), appSlug, }), });` — the credential-sync request has no authentication or integrity proof, allowing impersonation of another user’s token request if the endpoint trusts these fields.
